contributions.text: Presents Kothden, a test generator for Java that selects inputs by the mutants they kill, targeting surviving mutants.
contributions.quote: First, a generator that targets surviving mutants.

contributions.text: Adds a check that reruns each newly generated test to identify flaky tests, which are reported rather than discarded.
contributions.quote: Second, a check that reruns each new test to find flaky ones.

contributions.text: Reports an evaluation on 30 open-source Java projects.
contributions.quote: Third, an evaluation on 30 open-source projects.

evaluation.text: On 30 projects, faults were seeded with a different mutation tool than the guiding one, and Kothden and a random baseline got the same ten-minute budget. Kothden reported 18% more seeded faults; 42 flaky tests were reported, 37 confirmed by hand.
evaluation.quote: Kothden found 18 percent more seeded faults than the baseline.

prior_work.text: Relates its work to search-based test generation, which optimizes coverage without mutants; to mutation analysis studies that motivate using mutants; to flaky-test measurement studies; and to fuzzers, which share input mutation but target crashes.
prior_work.quote: Search-based test generation [1] optimizes coverage and does not use mutants.

closest_cited_work.text: The generator uses a genetic algorithm described as in the style of earlier search-based work, which the paper contrasts with its mutant-based guidance.
closest_cited_work.quote: using a genetic algorithm in the style of earlier work [1].
